Porsche Major vs Minor Service Explained “Major” and “minor” are workshop shorthand, not a substitute for the model-specific maintenance schedule. The correct scope is the set of items due by time, distance and recorded history. Read guide

Porsche PDK Service Intervals Guide PDK intervals and fluid/filter requirements vary by transmission application. A 911, Macan and Panamera should not receive advice based on one generic PDK number. Read guide

Porsche Oil Change Intervals UAE Use the time and distance interval specified for the exact engine and model year. Oil approval, level procedure and operating pattern matter as much as a headline mileage. Read guide

Porsche Maintenance Cost in Dubai: Key Factors A responsible guide cannot publish one invented Porsche maintenance price. Cost depends on the exact vehicle, due items, condition, parts route, access, fluids and supported procedures. Read guide
Porsche Battery Life in Dubai Battery life cannot be guaranteed by age alone. Heat, storage, short trips, electrical load, charging and battery type all affect condition. Read guide

How Dubai Heat Affects Porsche Cars Heat increases cooling and AC demand and can expose marginal batteries, seals, hoses, tyres and fluids. It does not prove every component needs early replacement. Read guide

Porsche AC Maintenance in Dubai AC maintenance begins with performance, airflow and leak assessment. Refrigerant should not be added automatically without confirming type, quantity and why charge was lost. Read guide

Porsche Cooling System Maintenance Guide Cooling maintenance is model-specific because a 911, Cayenne, hybrid and Taycan can contain very different circuits. Clean airflow and leak-free operation matter, but circuit work requires the correct procedure. Read guide
Porsche Brake Wear in Dubai Brake life depends on vehicle mass, fitted system, traffic, driving style, temperature and track use. Mileage alone cannot predict remaining pad or disc life. Read guide
Porsche Tyre Wear in Dubai Porsche tyre wear reflects pressure, alignment, suspension, wheel condition, driving load and on AWD vehicles the relationship between all four tyres. Read guide

Porsche Pre-Purchase Inspection Checklist UAE A Porsche PPI should identify the exact car, verify available history, scan relevant systems, inspect condition and document limitations. It cannot guarantee that no future fault will occur. Read guide

Buying a Used Porsche in Dubai Choose the individual car, not only the badge or advertised specification. Condition, records, accident repair, warnings, tyres and deferred maintenance can outweigh a lower purchase price. Read guide

Porsche Dealer vs Independent Specialist Dubai The right choice depends on warranty status, recall/campaign needs, required access, workshop capability, parts options and the specific job—not a blanket claim that one is always better. Read guide
Porsche Warning Lights Explained Colour, exact message and vehicle behaviour determine urgency. A warning identifies a system condition, not automatically the component to replace. Read guide
Common Porsche Problems in Dubai There is no responsible universal failure list for every Porsche. Owners more usefully browse by observed symptom, model and fitted system. Read guide

Porsche 718 Maintenance Guide UAE 718 maintenance differs between turbocharged flat-four and GT-oriented flat-six variants and between manual and PDK vehicles. Read guide

Weak AC or rising coolant temperature High ambient temperatures expose weak compressors, refrigerant leaks, restricted condensers, cooling fans, thermostats and coolant leaks. Early diagnosis matters before Dubai summer load increases. Read the weak-AC guide

title: Mercedes Problems & Diagnostic Guides | Digi-Tec Dubai
descriptions: Practical Mercedes owner guides for AIRMATIC, gearbox jerking, overheating, AC, oil leaks, no-start and battery warnings, with safe next steps.
headings: Mercedes Gearbox Jerking When Changing Gears
Return to the Mercedes-Benz service hub

internalContentLinks.anchor: Suspension Driving advice Mercedes AIRMATIC Malfunction An AIRMATIC warning means the suspension control system has detected a condition outside its expected range. It does not identify which component failed, and it does not automatically mean the compressor or all four air struts need replacement. Read diagnostic guide

Suspension Mercedes Suspension Dropping Overnight A Mercedes that sits lower after several hours is showing a height-retention symptom. On an air-equipped model, the pattern—one corner, one axle or the whole vehicle—helps direct leak testing, but the parked position alone does not prove which component is leaking. Read diagnostic guide

Transmission Mercedes Gearbox Jerking When Changing Gears “Jerking” can mean a sharp upshift, a thump into Drive, a bump during coast-down or a shudder under light acceleration. Those are different events. Identifying the gear, temperature, load and direction of torque is more useful than replacing parts from a code list. Read diagnostic guide

Transmission Driving advice Mercedes Transmission Slipping Transmission slip is a mismatch between engine speed and the vehicle acceleration or commanded gear. Owners may describe an RPM flare, delayed drive or loss of pull. It should be distinguished from a normal downshift, traction-control intervention or engine power fault. Read diagnostic guide

Engine & electrical Driving advice Mercedes Check Engine Light The check-engine light means the engine or emissions control has detected a fault that meets its reporting threshold. A steady light and a flashing light carry different urgency, while the stored code identifies the monitored condition—not automatically the failed part. Read diagnostic guide

Engine & electrical Driving advice Mercedes Engine Overheating Overheating means the cooling system is no longer controlling engine temperature under the current load. Continuing to drive can turn a hose, fan or pump fault into cylinder-head, turbocharger or lubrication damage. Read diagnostic guide

Climate Mercedes AC Not Cooling Weak Mercedes AC can be caused by refrigerant loss, inadequate condenser airflow, compressor control, pressure/temperature sensors, blower restriction or air-distribution faults. “Needs gas” is a symptom guess, not a leak diagnosis. Read diagnostic guide

Engine & electrical Mercedes Oil Leak Oil on the undertray or garage floor confirms leakage but not its origin. Mercedes undertrays and airflow can carry oil rearward, so diagnosis should start at the highest fresh wet point after the area is inspected and, when appropriate, cleaned. Read diagnostic guide

Engine & electrical Mercedes Won't Start The most useful first distinction is whether the engine does not crank, cranks at normal speed but does not start, cranks slowly, or starts and immediately stops. Each pattern leads to a different electrical, authorization, fuel or engine-management test path. Read diagnostic guide

Engine & electrical Driving advice Mercedes Battery Warning A Mercedes battery message can refer to low 12-volt state of charge, an auxiliary/backup battery function, a charging-system fault or, on equipped models, a 48-volt/DC-DC problem. Replacing the main battery without identifying the exact message can miss the fault. Read diagnostic guide

title: Porsche Problems & Warning Signs | Digi-Tec
descriptions: Diagnostic guides for Porsche transmission, engine, cooling, suspension, brake, battery, AC and model-specific symptoms.

internalContentLinks.anchor: Porsche PDK Jerking Repeated jerking can come from clutch control, adaptations, engine torque delivery, mounts, driveline play or internal transmission condition; one shift event does not identify the cause. Read diagnostic guide

Porsche PDK Slipping Slipping describes engine speed rising without matching acceleration or incomplete clutch engagement. It should be distinguished from a commanded downshift or traction intervention. Read diagnostic guide
Porsche PDK Warning Message A PDK warning reports a condition detected by the control system; the wording and stored event matter more than guessing a failed part. Read diagnostic guide

Porsche Delayed Gear Engagement A delay after selecting drive or reverse may involve transmission pressure, clutch or converter control, fluid, adaptations, mounts or engine operation depending on the fitted gearbox. Read diagnostic guide

Porsche Coolant Leak Coolant can escape from hoses, fittings, tanks, radiators, pumps, housings or other circuit components. The visible drip may be far from the highest fresh source. Read diagnostic guide

Porsche Engine Overheating Rising temperature can reflect coolant loss, poor circulation, airflow, fan control, thermostat or engine-management issues. Repeated top-ups are not a diagnosis. Read diagnostic guide
Porsche Oil Leak Oil may travel along covers, undertrays and airflow, so the lowest wet point rarely proves which seal or housing is leaking. Read diagnostic guide

Porsche Excessive Oil Consumption Consumption must be measured over a known distance with the correct level procedure. External leakage and inaccurate readings should be excluded first. Read diagnostic guide
Porsche Engine Misfire A misfire is incomplete combustion in one or more cylinders. The code identifies the detected event, not automatically a coil or spark plug. Read diagnostic guide

Porsche Check Engine Light The warning shows that engine or emissions control detected an event. Severity depends on whether it is steady or flashing and how the vehicle behaves. Read diagnostic guide

Porsche PASM Fault A PASM fault can involve controlled dampers, sensors, wiring, power supply, calibration or another chassis module. It does not automatically mean the damper has failed. Read diagnostic guide
Porsche PDCC Fault PDCC faults differ between hydraulic and electromechanical system generations. The platform must be identified before testing. Read diagnostic guide

Porsche Suspension Dropping Overnight A corner or axle that loses height while parked suggests air loss or control behaviour, but the leak source must be isolated before replacing parts. Read diagnostic guide
Porsche Air Suspension Warning The warning may involve pressure, compressor temperature, a leak, valve, sensor, supply voltage or control communication. Read diagnostic guide
Porsche Brake Warning Light Brake warnings can indicate pad wear, fluid level, parking-brake, ABS/stability or hydraulic concerns. Colour and exact wording matter. Read diagnostic guide
Porsche Battery Warning A battery warning may concern charging, state of charge, current monitoring, wiring or another low-voltage supply issue—not just battery age. Read diagnostic guide
Porsche Won't Start Separate no-crank, crank-no-start and powers-up-but-will-not-ready conditions. Each points to a different diagnostic path. Read diagnostic guide
Porsche AC Not Cooling Weak AC can result from refrigerant loss, poor condenser airflow, compressor control, sensors, valves, blower or air-distribution faults. Read diagnostic guide
Porsche Steering Vibration Vibration may come from tyres, wheels, hubs, brakes, bearings, suspension or driveline. Speed and braking dependence help separate causes. Read diagnostic guide

Porsche Macan Transfer Case Symptoms Low-speed shudder, binding or vibration can involve PTM/transfer hardware, but tyres, wheel circumference, PDK, mounts and engine operation must be excluded. Read diagnostic guide
Porsche Cayenne Air Suspension Problems Cayenne height loss, slow lifting or compressor warnings need leak and pressure testing matched to the fitted generation. Read diagnostic guide

Porsche 911 Cooling Problems 911 cooling concerns vary across 997, 991 and 992 and between Carrera, Turbo and GT engines. Front airflow, multiple circuits and leak location must be considered. Read diagnostic guide
Porsche Taycan Charging Problems A charging failure can originate in the vehicle, cable, connector, AC/DC supply, charging station, communication or thermal conditions. Read diagnostic guide

Porsche Taycan 12V Battery Problems The 12-volt system wakes and controls vehicle electronics; a low-voltage failure can prevent the high-voltage system from becoming ready even when the traction battery is charged. Read diagnostic guide

title: Porsche Systems Explained | Digi-Tec Dubai
descriptions: Understand Porsche PDK, Tiptronic, PASM, PDCC, PCCB, air suspension, Sport Chrono, rear-axle steering and PTM systems.

internalContentLinks.anchor: Porsche PDK Porsche Doppelkupplungsgetriebe is a dual-clutch transmission. Two clutch paths allow one gear to transmit torque while the next gear is prepared, but PDK design and service requirements vary by model and generation. Read guide

Porsche Tiptronic Tiptronic is Porsche terminology used with conventional automatic transmissions that include manual driver selection. It is not PDK: it generally uses a torque converter and planetary gearsets. Read guide

Porsche PASM Porsche Active Suspension Management electronically adjusts damper behaviour. PASM does not automatically mean air suspension: many PASM vehicles use steel springs with electronically controlled dampers. Read guide

Porsche PDCC Porsche Dynamic Chassis Control is an active anti-roll system designed to reduce body roll. Hardware and operating principle vary by platform, so hydraulic and electromechanical applications should not be treated as identical. Read guide

Porsche PCCB Porsche Ceramic Composite Brake uses ceramic-composite discs with compatible pads and model-specific hardware. PCCB condition and replacement decisions should not be based on the same visual assumptions or simple thickness checks used for iron discs. Read guide

Porsche Air Suspension Porsche air suspension replaces conventional coil springs with pneumatic spring elements and adds compressors, reservoirs, valves, lines, sensors and electronic control. PASM may be integrated but is not the same system. Read guide

Porsche Sport Chrono Sport Chrono is an equipment package whose functions vary by model and generation. It can change drive modes and powertrain or chassis responses; the dashboard clock is only the most visible element. Read guide

Porsche Rear-Axle Steering Rear-axle steering changes rear-wheel angle by a small amount. At lower speeds it can improve manoeuvrability; at higher speeds it can support stability. Fitment and control strategy vary by model. Read guide

Porsche PTM & AWD Porsche Traction Management describes model-dependent all-wheel-drive control. Hardware differs across 911, Cayenne, Macan and Panamera platforms, so PTM is not one universal transfer case. Read guide
